chapter_note: Chapter 18 is overwhelmingly substrate teaching: the systematic enumeration of the Five Wars between the Sons of Light and Sons of Darkness, structured as a numbered cosmic-historical sequence (First Living Man, Living Spirit, Third Ambassador, Jesus the Splendor/Glorious One, and the eschatological fifth war). Teaching purity is exceptionally high (0.948). The chapter is severely damaged (98.7%), but what survives is dense substrate cosmology: First Man's tree, the Living Soul, the Virgin/Living Fire, binding of archons in five worlds, three strongholds, the Image of the Third Messenger, archonic host, the cosmic Jesus the Glorious, the Call and Answer, the hope of Adam. Two clear editorial intrusions: i=3 carries the formulaic "the Illuminator" attribution (mixed — strip frame, keep the war-sequence opening); i=17–18 contain a Gospel citation by "the Savior" (axe at the root of the tree) introduced by "as the Savior said" — classic LATE citation-formula intrusion. The "Jesus the Glorious" of i=51 is the Manichaean cosmic Splendor, not Gospel Jesus — substrate. i=74 ("every elect who shall...") flagged because ⲉⲕⲗⲉⲕⲧⲟⲥ is normally an ecclesial marker, but here in eschatological-war context it functions as substratic category; kept as substrate with note. Editorial fatigue score is negative — substrate vocabulary actually drops in second half due to severity of damage rather than editorial drift.
